summary: The bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the FDA to grant marketing approval within 30 days for any drug, biologic, or device already lawfully sold in the UK or a listed developed country, unless the agency affirmatively finds it unsafe or ineffective.

scores.thoughts: The bill modifies FDA regulatory procedures for product approvals but contains no provisions that authorize, expand, or reduce federal expenditures. Fee provisions treat requests equivalently to existing applications without altering overall spending levels.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.

The core of the bill amends the FD&C Act to create a reciprocal marketing approval pathway that deems foreign-authorized drugs, biologics, and devices as FDA-approved if safety/effectiveness criteria and unmet-need conditions are met. This directly alters the regulatory framework governing market entry of medical products, reducing domestic approval barriers and facilitating private-sector commercialization.
No provisions relate to firearms, ammunition, or gun regulations.
No immigration, visa, border, or residency provisions are present.
The bill addresses general drug and device approvals without targeting abortifacients, reproductive medications, or abortion-related access.
No defense, military, or national security spending or policy elements exist.
No environmental, emissions, or regulatory provisions concerning climate or natural resources.
No welfare, entitlement, or benefits program changes are included.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy provisions.
The bill concerns FDA marketing approval for legitimate pharmaceutical products; it does not address controlled-substance scheduling, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal procedure reforms.
While the bill references foreign marketing authorizations, it does not alter tariffs, trade agreements, import quotas, or protectionist measures.
No deficit, debt ceiling, or fiscal-balance provisions.
No civil-rights, nondiscrimination, or LGBTQ-specific legal protections addressed.
No foreign assistance, aid appropriations, or international development measures.
No voting rights, election administration, or campaign provisions.
No data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance provisions.
No labor, union, or employment-law changes.
No religious exemptions, conscience protections, or civil-rights balancing provisions.
